claims.claim: Reviewers describe the onboarding experience as confusing and overwhelming for new players, with unguided quests and unclear directions on where to go.

citations.review_text: i could only play at a little and i will explain why: i got spawned, i got some directions. The game was fun and all... then the next thing that happens is that i have no idea what to do. I was spammed with lot of things that are not understanable and i got overwhelmed to quit. This is not a game that makes you grow within the pass of time, it feels like it throws at all at you at once and you are unable to understand whats going on.  But the little i played it was fun, so anyone that can the patience to go out and find a manual for each thing will surely enjoy it... but not me, i have not enough autism for it.
The gunplay is top notch, but it is basically impossible to understand for a new player what to do or where to go. It's like trying to understand a movie by watching only the last 5 minutes
tried to play this with my son this game is too hard to navigate , too many maps and quests telling you to go to many places all at once

claims.claim: Reviewers note that original campaigns and locations, including the Red War, have been removed from the game.

citations.review_text:
Played 500+ hours of this on PSN, got it day 1 after being a player on D1. Shame you cant still play Warmind or the red war, those expansions had some cool sections, (like red wars opening, the worm god fight)
Stopped playing just after shadowkeep dropped, but got the witch Queen and the final shape for 4 bucks to play through and see the story line end. Just went through Beyond lights campaign and remembered why I found this gameloop so addictive, and now I can play these DLC without FOMO or really excessive grinding, I just loaded up some of my old favourite guns (rat king, hardlight, misfit, braytech werewolf, so many kickass weapons) and am enjoying having one last run through with this game and series which I am super fond of. I started playing destiny before my son was born and now im finishing it off with him joining in, crazy to think how many years I played and enjoyed this game. Thanks destiny for all the laughs, Frustration, dopamine, friendships, and all the fun times. Going to play through these DLCs, hit a few games of crucible and then call it.
Thanks for the memories, gaurdians, my ghost can rest soon.
Only get it on a sale. The best content has been vaulted(removed). Its a fun first playthrough but I wouldn't suggest grinding it

WARNING FOR NEW PLAYERS!!!!  I as a new player was looking forward to playing destiny 2 start to finish... Sadly I cannot do so, not because of hardware limitations on my part but Bungie has actually removed the Red war campaign (which if i'm not mistaken is the original destiny 2 story) along with purging 2 or 3 of the story DLC, this means that new players like us are lore gated, we can only experience the original story through old youtube videos, no red war no curse of osiris and no war mind, they even removed 5 entire destinations including mars, mercury, io, titan and the leviathen. It's a huge buzz kill to be gate kept like this and they didnt even do a particularly good job cleaning up the story for new players, yes we have a new into area, and new intros to the commands of the faction but go far enough in and they will start talking to you as if you have always been their greatest ally and a war hero despite us not being present in the Red war... Of course this is ignoring how unfair it is to delete content other people paid for. The worst part is the new stories would have been perfectly good as a new separate game or if they transferred the old story stuff to a single player version of destiny to where previous owners get a copy for free (so they don't lose the stuff they already paid for) but is still sold to new players allowing them to play the original story. My opologies for whining I'm just frustrated, I'm here to play a game not watch potentially 30 hrs of youtube videos to understand the lore before i can come into destiny 2 and understand what is actually going on.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the onboarding and progression for new players as overly complicated and lacking clear explanations of core systems.

citations.review_text:
Destiny 2 has some of the best gunplay and combat I've experienced in an FPS game. The raids, dungeons, and co-op activities can be incredibly fun with friends.

Unfortunately, the game is just too complicated for new and returning players. There are too many systems, currencies, quests, menus, and expansions thrown at you with very little explanation. I constantly felt like I needed YouTube guides, Discord servers, and third-party tools just to understand what I should be doing next. This confusion has been a common criticism among players and gaming media for years.

Instead of spending my time playing the game, I often found myself searching for information outside the game. If a game requires Discord, guides, and community explanations to understand its core progression, that's a problem.

Great gameplay, but the onboarding and overall complexity made it difficult for me to enjoy.

Amazing combat. Confusing everything else.

It's a gigantic ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ of a game
- loading times are excessively long
- there's too much of everything and nothing is explained, as soon as you log in you're litteraly crushed by 10 years of upgrades piling down on your head with absolutely zero explanation of what to do
- don't get me started on PvP where any notion of match making is absolutely forsaken and you can play against overstuffed max level players on your first day as a rookie
- And let's end by mentioning all the bugs, loots not being attributed, ranks and quests not validating.

If you're ready to bang your head on a wall while navigating one hundred different menu to get to understand anything this is the game for you !

Onboarding/New Player Experience needs a lotta work. Make the main storyline more blatantly ordered and handholdy regarding what to do next, and it's golden. Other than that it's like high fantasy Halo and I love that. 
Shame they had to do final update, but at least in its current state it's p fun!

I only have a couple hundred hours across D1 and D2, but that was some rock solid gameplay back then right there. Same here, but several years after launch it's a tangled and confusing mess for anyone to start.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the new player experience is poor, poorly explaining mechanics, failing to teach important systems, or leaving players confused.

citations.review_text:
I'm a bit late to the "review the death of the game" party but I'll TRY keep it short (lmao I didn't).

This game was a rollercoaster over the years. It was awesome, it sucked, it had the best content, it had the worst, it was all over the place, but at the end of the day it was always something that myself and my friends could come back to every year (and sometimes every few months) and have some really cool and fun experiences together (as everyone says, the raids/dungeons are just some of the best gaming content ever imo especially when you do them blind with friends).

The last update has been really cool, though personally for me it's been tough wanting to log-in given there's nothing coming "after". I did log a good number of hours in the first few days, experimenting with new builds, etc., and I will likely log back in at some point when friends are ready to knockout raids/dungeons we haven't done. But for now, sorta just sitting on the sidelines.

I may not have as many hours on this game as others, though I would say it's not because I didn't want to play, but because there were so many times throughout the game's life where I WANTED to play, but man there was just no reason or incentive to (which sucked). That being said, as a Destiny 1 launch-day OG, Destiny is, was, and will probably forever be in my top 10 games for who knows how long.

If you're a new player, I would definitely recommend giving it a try. The new player experience is absolutely awful and you WILL get bombarded with so much nonsense that is confusing, but if you can work passed that or play with a friend, you're probably find that the overall gameplay and things to do can be very fun (though I would avoid PvP especially now that the game has minimal updates/support - it's bound to only get worse sadly...)

If you're a vet that has played somewhat recently (last ~6 months), I still think it's worth checking out the update though admittedly you probably will only get about a few weeks or m…

Having played thousands of hours on PlayStation across both Destiny and Destiny 2, the end of content updates for Destiny 2 is bittersweet as whilst Destiny 2 is full of content, empty areas in the game world, in game dialogue and unachievable titles serve as a reminder of the wealth of missing content and a story best served by YouTube.

With the introduction of the Destiny Content Vault, the reworked onboarding experience does a terrible job of introducing players to key characters and mechanics and the remaining campaigns can be hard to locate via the director with little guidance as to what and when they should be completed. Bizarrely some key campaign quest lines remain time gated – refreshing on the weekly reset. This leads to a frustrating experience for new players as they try to find there way in this convoluted mess whilst picking up loot left by players blasting through group content like fear of missing out (FOMO) still exists.

Destiny 2 will be remembered for some truly epic moments, and no other game has captured my imagination in the same way. Unfortunately, Destiny 2 is now essentially a checkbox exercise – collecting the gear, triumphs and titles remaining with those guardians still clinging on to Destiny of old.

There's a REALLY good game here under a REALLY rough start and it's best experienced with a guiding hand. The campaigns range from hilariously bad to genuinely enjoyable but unfortunately the new player experience will filter out 80-90% of players because it teaches nothing important or repeats itself for no discernable reason.

If you can get past it you'll find a game that has one of the best looter shooter experiences and some remarkably deep buildcrafting options. Every class branches out in so many different ways that you WILL find something that clicks and makes you go "That's it. That's me." Also the raid and dungeon experiences. Nothing else I've played has come close to replicating these experiences. If you can find 5 other people to play with I absolutely recommend playing these.

claims.claim: Reviewers point out that understanding quests and progressing requires looking up outside guides because in-game directions and explanations are obscure.

citations.review_text:
I recommend this game with a big fat asterisk* ... you have to look up guides a lot. This game is the most fun I've had playing a shooter, but omg the devs SUCK at telling the player what to do. Every quest description is like, "Go to (insert random bull crap name of a random lore thing) at (insert bull crap location that you can't navigate to because you don't recognize the name). I've played for 120 hours, then 15 hours has been me being AFK looking up all the obscure stuff in the game that isn't explained well. That makes this game both wonderful and extremely hard to learn. I just barely wrapped my head around all the things I am ABLE to do in the game, but I'm still figuring out how to ACTUALLY DO THEM. However... when I do figure out the obscure stuff, it feels great. I ended up liking all the obscure stuff, it's just hard to understand what it all means at first... but after you understand, it's super cool. 

The multiplayer is awesome and has a really high skill ceiling. I've had pretty good matchmaking for the most part. There are a lot of people playing right now, so it's easy to find games. Same thing with raids, because they have mechanics in the game that let you join a team of 6 random people and play a raid together. 

The solo content is really fun. I loved Beyond Light and enjoyed all 20 hours of it. I liked Renegades and it's fun to play with friends. Shadowkeep was definitely the worst when it comes to not knowing what to do so it was frustrating to look up guides on YouTube every 5 seconds... but the boss fights were pretty cool. 

In short... I think you can have a lot of fun with this game if you're brave enough to get over the freaking ginormous learning curve.

citations.review_text: They vaulted everything for new players, and its just too convoluted to even understand how to progress. Gunplay is amazing though

Destiny 2 has always been one of those games that hits deeper than it should. The gunplay is still unmatched with it's clean, weighty, and satisfying in a way that makes every fight feel intentional. Even after all these years, dropping into a strike or loading into the EDZ still gives that familiar feeling of “yeah, this is home.” It’s a game built on atmosphere, music, and moments that stick with you long after you log off.

That’s why it’s genuinely sad seeing development shut down under Sony. Destiny 2 deserved a better future than being quietly shelved. There’s so much heart in this game in the worlds, the characters, the raids, the community and it hurts knowing that the momentum just stopped instead of being given a real send‑off. It feels like losing a place you used to visit, not just a game you used to play.

And honestly, there were so many ways Destiny 2 could’ve kept growing. An offline mode with bot teammates for raids and dungeons would’ve been huge. Not everyone has a full fireteam on standby, and the big set‑pieces are some of the best content Bungie ever made. Being able to experience those moments solo, even with AI help, would’ve kept the game alive for a lot of people who just want to enjoy the world at their own pace.

If anyone ever picks up Destiny 2 again in the future, I hope they bring back the OG Red War campaign. It was the perfect introduction: simple, structured, emotional, and it gave new players a real foundation instead of dropping them into chaos. Destiny has always been at its best when it gives you a clear path and lets you grow into your power. Red War did that better than anything that came after.

Even with all its flaws, Destiny 2 is special. It’s a game that meant something to people; a place to unwind, a place to chase loot, a place to feel powerful, a place to hang out with friends. And maybe one day, someone will pick it back up and give it the future it deserved. Until then, it’s still worth remembering for what …
